To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we develop a "thing-adaptation" online saddle-point algorithm that is suitable for online convex optimization with temporally-varying constraints, and that we prove it yields desirable performance.

we develop a novel online saddle-point algorithm for fog offloading that automatically adjusts the learning rate to offer desirable task performance, and we prove its convergence in terms of dynamic regret and fit.

we propose a novel online convex optimization framework for fog computing in IoT; we develop an online saddle-point algorithm that is "thing-adaptive", i.e., it automatically adjusts the step size to offer the desirable learning rate; we prove that our algorithm yields sub-linear dynamic regret, which generalizes the widely-used static regret, and dynamic fit; we show via simulations that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in fog offloading problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
online learning for "thing-adaptive'' Fog Computing in IoT.
a new online learning paradigm for "thing-adaptive” fog computing.
the development and analysis of an online saddle-point scheme for time-varying problems with long-term constraints.

the present work is a significant advance in online optimization for Fog Computing, as it offers a general and efficient approach to learning in the IoT.
the TAOSP scheme offers a promising solution to the emerging problem of online learning for "thing-adaptive” fog computing in IoT.
our TAOSP scheme is able to offer a sub-linear dynamic regret while simultaneously keeping a sub-linear dynamic fit, which is a desirable feature for online learning in fog computing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a new online learning framework for Fog computing and the IoT that is capable of handling both the dynamic nature of the tasks and the heterogeneous systems involved.
the proposed TAOSP scheme offers a new way of online learning that is particularly suitable for fog computing and other IoT applications.

, by combining online convex optimization and the saddle-point framework, our TAOSP approach is able to provide an efficient online solution for "thing-adaptive” tasks in IoT, which are characterized by temporally unpredictable availability, heterogeneous resources and time-varyning constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online learning in IoT can be made more efficient, by automatically adjusting to the temporal variations of resources.

the proposed online saddle-point scheme is capable of learning from data and adapting to the dynamics of the problem, which makes the approach appealing for the emerging IoT applications in fog computing.
online convex optimization is a promising approach for fog computing, and can be tailored for the IoT.
